references.text: Isaiah 5:1-7 contains a parable about a vineyard that God expected to bear good fruit but instead produced bad fruit. This is a direct parallel to the parable Jesus tells in Mark 12:9, where the owner of the vineyard (God) will ultimately destroy the unfruitful workers (Israel's leaders) and give the vineyard to others (Gentiles or believers outside Israel's physical descendants).

Matthew 21:33-41 gives a parallel account to Mark 12:9, where Jesus tells the same parable about the vineyard, and the listeners give an answer similar to the conclusion in Mark, indicating that the owner of the vineyard will destroy the wicked workers and give the vineyard to others.

Luke 20:9-16 also gives a parallel account to Mark 12:9, where Jesus tells the parable about the vineyard. Luke's version of the parable ends with Jesus saying that God will give the vineyard to others, which emphasizes the same point as in Mark.
